texts.title: Emergency Powers
texts.body: The Senate has voted {holder.name} of {holder.house} its emergency powers. For three years the other consul's veto is set aside, no election will be held, the Senate will lean toward whatever {holder.name} moves, and money can be levied from every house without a vote. It was done lawfully, because the Reach is in danger. Everyone in the chamber knows how such things have ended elsewhere.

choices.stand_with_them: Say they should be helped to carry it.
choices.warn_the_senate: Say what three years has a way of becoming.

texts.title: The Powers Are Yours
texts.body: The Senate has voted you its emergency powers. For three years your colleague's veto is set aside and you may strike a motion every year; the Senate leans toward what you move; you may levy on the houses without a vote; and no election will be held. When the term is up, or the danger is past, you are to lay them down.

choices.swear_to_lay_them_down: Swear, unasked, to lay them down when it is over.
choices.take_them_and_say_nothing: Thank the Senate, and say nothing about when.

texts.title: The Term Is Up
texts.body: The powers are due to be laid down. You can lay them down, and be remembered for it. You can ask the Senate for more time, if the danger is still there. Or you can simply keep them: each year you do costs you the Reach's trust and the regard of every house, and after three the Senate will take them. One who has held them past the first term may also put it to the Senate that they be held for life.

texts.title: A Year Past Leave
texts.body: You have held the emergency powers a year past the Senate's leave. Nobody has been sent to take them from you. A delegation has come instead, to ask when.

choices.face_them_down: Receive them standing, and give no answer.
choices.give_way: Tell them: at the year's end.

texts.title: A Levy Without a Vote
texts.body: {holder.name} of {holder.house} has levied on every house of the Reach by the emergency powers, for the fleets. No vote was taken. The collectors have been to your house and gone.

choices.pay_and_say_so: Let it be known you paid gladly.
choices.pay_and_protest: Enter a protest in the record.

texts.title: The Powers Laid Down
texts.body: {holder.name} of {holder.house} has laid down the emergency powers and taken a consul's chair again, one of two. The Republic has what it lent back.

choices.note_it: Note that it can be done.

texts.title: You Laid Them Down
texts.body: It is done. The powers are the Senate's again, the other consul's veto is restored, and an election will be called. You held all of it and gave it back.

choices.stay_and_serve: Take your chair again in the morning.

texts.title: Stripped of the Powers
texts.body: The Senate has ended the emergency powers itself. It was not your doing and everyone knows it. Your house has lost standing, the heads of the others think worse of you, and it will be a long time before a Senate trusts your house with them again.

choices.remember_who_voted: Ask for the roll of the vote.
